title: Probe False-Positives x Automated Steering: When a Noisy Monitor Triggers Harmful Over-Correction

original_idea.body: Probe false positives trigger unwarranted steering that itself causes harm; compose an expected-harm estimate from monitor error and actuator harm.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible monitor-error-becomes-harm chain, but depends on automated steering being deployed; modest gap to catastrophic risk.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Probe FPR + apply steering on FPs + expected-harm bookkeeping; guided, novice + mentor feasible.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused deliverable but combines probe eval, steering harm measurement, and a composition step.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Risk-budget framing for automated steering harnesses is foundational, lab-deprioritized infra; no internal access.

low_compute.reasoning: Inference + cheap probe on one small model; single GPU.

novelty.reasoning: The expected-harm composition of monitor-error x actuator-harm appears largely novel.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Composing probe false-positive rate with steering-actuator harm into a single risk budget is an underexplored framing.
